ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit PEP database, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and SIFA domestic sanctions and restrictive measures list; ongoing transaction monitoring and adverse-media screening are required under the Anti-Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Financing Act 2007.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) — Registrar of International Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the International Companies Act 1987, the statutory name must be in English or Samoan and shall be recorded in the Latin script. A Chinese-character trading name is permitted as a parallel business name in the constitutional documents and may appear on commercial invoices, but it is not the registered name. The registered Latin transliteration must be used for all SIFA filings and statutory notices, and the Chinese name must not be confusingly similar to any existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may apply to the Registrar of International Companies for a single extension of the name reservation no later than 14 days before expiry, with the extension granted upon payment of the statutory fee. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written objection with the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice. The Registrar must determine the objection within 10 working days. A further administrative appeal lies to the Minister responsible for the International Companies Act 1987, and a final appeal on a point of law may be brought to the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. Every Samoa International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the office of a licensed international company service provider registered with SIFA. The office must be capable of receiving legal process and official correspondence. Use of a post-office box, virtual office, or forwarding address does not satisfy section 7 of the International Companies Act 1987.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. For a standard low-risk retail IoT holding company, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by SIFA or the corporate service provider's own compliance module is 5–10% during the first three years; the probability may increase to 20% if the provider is placed under enhanced supervisory review or if adverse AML/CFT intelligence is received.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies Amendment Acts 2008, 2016 and 2020), ss. 4-11 (incorporation), s. 58 (registered office), s. 74 (registered agent), ss. 84-92 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form IC-1) together with Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent (Form IC-2), endorsed by a SIFA-licensed international company service provider
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized capital may be expressed in any freely convertible currency and is declared in the Memorandum; no escrow or deposit account is required; annual government license fee is separate and calculated on authorized capital bands
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscriber shares in the authorized capital of the Company be allotted to the subscribers named in the Memorandum of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the licensed agent be appointed registered agent of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors named herein be and are hereby appointed as the first directors of the Company, each to hold office until removed by the Board. RESOLVED FURTHER that any one director be authorized to execute banking mandates, retain e-commerce payment providers, and complete all statutory filings with SIFA in connection with these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed International Company Service Provider (Registrar-approved agent), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFA-licensed agent via engagement letter and power of attorney. The agent confirms the availability of its Apia address as the statutory registered office and undertakes to file the agent declaration with SIFA. Provide certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and a professional reference for each proposed director and shareholder.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney in favor of licensed agent
Certified passport copy of each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
Proposed beneficial ownership information for SIFA internal records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent declines the file, appoint an alternative SIFA-licensed agent and re-execute the power of attorney; no SIFA record is affected until submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed agent to submit two preferred company names to SIFA for availability review. Names must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or the abbreviation thereof, and must not conflict with existing Samoa domestic or international entities or contain restricted words unless consent is obtained.
required_dossiers: Two proposed company names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, the agent resubmits with alternative names; if the name is objectionable, a written explanation and a fresh application with a substituted name is filed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed agent acting as subscriber signatory; notarization not mandatory under Samoan law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association incorporating the object clause for retailing smart home IoT hardware and home automation devices through e-commerce channels, and confirm the authorized share capital, subscriber details, and share classes. Each subscriber executes the Memorandum as a deed; the agent countersigns as witness.
required_dossiers: Consent of each subscriber to take shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries the constitution, amend the Memorandum via supplementary filing or re-execute the document; SIFA rules allow a correction notice to be confirmed within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to Registrar and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent files the executed Memorandum and Articles via SIFA's electronic lodgment portal together with Forms IC-1 and IC-2, the name reservation confirmation, and the prescribed fee. SIFA registers the company and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Memorandum and Articles of Association)
Form IC-2 (Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete execution, cure by filing a correcting statement or re-executed page within 10 business days; if SIFA rejects the filing, request a written notice of refusal and resubmit after rectification with no re-imposition of the full incorporation fee for correcting the same file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Officer Appointments, and Corporate Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company; corporate records maintained by the licensed agent in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by written resolution. Adopt the first board resolution to allot subscriber shares, establish the registered office and agent, and appoint directors and officers. Open the statutory registers (members, directors, charges), prepare share certificates, and issue a Certificate of Incumbency for banking and e-commerce payment provider onboarding.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (each director)
Register of members and share certificate
Certificate of Incumbency issued by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer appointment is defective, the Board may ratify by a fresh written resolution; a corrected Certificate of Incumbency is issued by the agent within 2 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Samoa International Companies are offshore-exempt entities prohibited from carrying on physical business or holding land in Samoa (International Companies Act 1987, s. 153), apart from leasing office premises through the registered agent
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No local operating license required; the offshore International Company conducts only cross-border e-commerce retail of smart home IoT hardware, which is outside Samoa's domestic trade licensing regime

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical industrial operations, manufacturing, or warehouse facilities in Samoa; pure digital retail model with third-party logistics; no EIA report or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation in Samoa; if any future physical warehouse were established in Samoa, compliance with the Water Resources Management Act 2008, the Waste Management Act 2005, and the E-waste Regulations would be triggered, with e-waste from returned IoT devices routed to certified recycling only

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required — the company maintains no physical workplace or retail premises in Samoa; the registered office is the licensed agent's professional suite. If a future Samoan office space were leased, the tenant would require a PUMA building occupancy permit, a fire clearance from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA), and occupational safety registration under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Samoa (valaisi o Tupe Mau, official portal https://www.revenue.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Samoa International Company, the company automatically obtains a Certificate of Incorporation from the Samoa International Companies Registrar (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour). To procure a statutory Tax Identification Number, the IC or its registered agent must file an application with the Ministry for Revenue, providing the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office address in Samoa, and details of the authorised representative. The Ministry for Revenue issues a TIN in the format of nine digits. The registered agent must maintain the physical presence requirements and notify the Ministry for Revenue of any changes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa International Companies are statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax, VAT, and stamp duty. No check-the-box election exists under Samoan domestic law. An IC may, by issuing a formal notice to the Ministry for Revenue, voluntarily file for tax residence if it intends to claim treaty benefits, but the default position is automatic tax exemption for offshore income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 per annum of taxable turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force for Samoa. Invoices may be issued in paper or electronic format and must contain the supplier's VAGST registration number, date, description, and amount of tax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods and certain services supplied for direct export outside Samoa qualify for zero-rating at 0% VAGST, provided the exporter is a registered person and holds evidence that the goods have been physically removed from Samoa within 90 days of supply. Offshore services supplied to non-residents are generally treated as outside the scope of VAGST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusDEC) duly stamped by the Samoa Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing removal from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation showing receipt of foreign currency
Proof of export under the VAGST regulations (Form VAGST-E)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit export claims retroactively within the statutory limitation period. Any fraudulent claim for zero-rating, misrepresentation of export documents, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days is punishable as a tax offence under the Tax Administration Act 2012, exposing the IC to a clawback of the wrongly claimed zero-rated input credits, a penalty of up to 150% of the tax evaded, and imprisonment of up to 10 years for responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) - Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, acting jointly with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for offshore/international company registration and AML/CFT supervision; the Exchange Control Act 1975 and Exchange Control Regulations 1978 are administered exclusively by the CBS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float with current-account convertibility available through CBS-licensed authorized dealers upon presentation of standard trade or service documentation. Capital-account transactions generally require CBS approval for resident entities, but the Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from the Exchange Control Act and may lawfully conduct all treasury operations in USD or any permitted foreign currency. Profit remittance, capital repatriation, and dividend distribution by the IC are unrestricted and carry no conversion obligation. Practical constraints: WST liquidity is thin, USD settlement requires correspondent banks in Australia or the United States, and counterparties in the local market may require a letter of comfort from the Samoan registered agent confirming the IC's non-resident exchange-control exempt status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must repatriate export proceeds and surrender them to an authorized dealer within 90 days from the date of shipment, with conversion into WST at the prevailing CBS reference rate unless a specific exemption is granted by the CBS. The Samoa International Company is treated as a non-resident for exchange-control purposes and is expressly exempt from surrender and mandatory conversion requirements, retaining a 100% foreign-currency retention ratio in its USD/heavy operational and escrow accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited, Samoa Branch (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
USD Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Domestic Retail Account Only (not suited for offshore IC structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium direct viability. Stripe and Shopify Payments maintain no licensed merchant-acquiring presence in Samoa and will not settle directly into a Samoan IC account without a verified Merchant of Record (MoR) arrangement. Offshore digital EMIs such as Payoneer and WorldFirst may onboard the entity for collections, but payouts are restricted to SWIFT transfers with fee deductions and may trigger enhanced due diligence at the receiving Samoan bank. Recommended architecture: retain BSP Samoa or ANZ Samoa as the primary USD settlement account, use an offshore payment aggregator/MoR for card-acquiring, and execute daily MT103 sweeps into the Samoan IC account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for first-time account opening. At least one director or a fully authorized signatory holding a notarized power of attorney must attend an in-person interview at the bank's Apia branch, provide original signature specimens, and execute the banking mandate. Remote opening is permitted only after preliminary in-country compliance clearance; all corporate documents must be notarized, apostilled, and certified by a SIFA-licensed registered agent, and director identification must be verified against a valid passport with a notarized English translation if required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-haven and shell-company profiling stemming from Samoa's offshore IC regime and the jurisdiction's historical inclusion on the FATF grey list (2018-2021).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA-issued Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; current registered-agent confirmation from the SIFA-licensed agent; audited or management financial statements; economic substance declaration and filing; board resolution approving the banking relationship; director CVs evidencing genuine IoT retail and distribution experience; enforceable supplier and customer contracts for Smart Home IoT devices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity and legacy bearer-share risk under older International Company structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete and updated register of beneficial owners filed with the Samoan registered agent; statutory declaration of beneficial ownership executed by each shareholder/director; undertaking to keep the share register and UBO register physically available at the agent's Apia office; bank reference letters from the directors' home-jurisdiction financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source and purpose of inbound shareholder capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share subscription agreement; board resolution approving capital contribution; remitter bank statements showing source of wealth; wealth-evidence pack (investment statements, title deeds, prior-year tax assessments); SWIFT reference matching; written anti-money-laundering communication with the receiving bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) prior to transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce payouts from unrelated global payment platforms (Stripe, Shopify Payments) flagged as potentially layering proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreement and Payment Service Agreement with the planned MoR/payment processor; monthly platform settlement statements; transaction-level reconciliation reports; documented refund and chargeback policy; jurisdiction-of-sale invoice register; live commercial website and marketplace listings evidencing genuine IoT hardware retail activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders execute inbound remittances in USD via SWIFT MT103 to the IC's Capital Escrow Account at BSP Samoa or ANZ Bank Samoa, using the remittance narrative 'Share Capital Contribution' accompanied by the IC registration number. The receiving bank will complete the inward-investment statistical declaration to the CBS and may require an IC Certificate and SIFA registration confirmation to validate the exchange-control exemption. Funds are held in escrow until the signatory directors confirm the receipt, after which the bank releases the capital into the operational USD account with no mandatory conversion into WST.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for Smart Home IoT hardware procurement from suppliers in China, Hong Kong, and Southeast Asia are executed in USD via SWIFT MT103 from the operational account at BSP Samoa or ANZ Samoa, supported by commercial invoices and packing lists. For high-value purchase orders exceeding USD 25,000, irrevocable sight documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 are recommended, with the bank acting as advising/issuing bank and settlement occurring through its Australian or US correspondent network. In-country USD clearing is unavailable; all cross-border payments route through SWIFT, while domestic WST clearance runs through the Samoa Interbank Settlement System (SISS).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/WST forward contracts with licensed CBS-authorized commercial banks (executed on a documented trade-deal basis with underlying commercial exposure).

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing the WST rate, available only through offshore counterparties where permitted by the IC's non-resident exchange-control exemption and not executed with a Samoan domestic bank.
Cross-currency swap between USD and WST with an offshore investment-grade counterparty for IC treasury purposes, subject to CBS authorized-dealer intermediation if any Samoan branch is involved.
Natural hedging via matched USD receivables and USD payables, maintained through segregated USD operational and settlement accounts with no conversion to WST.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months following each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to WST 500 (approx. USD 185); continued default for 6 months triggers administrative strike-off by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Fee (International Company Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts penalty of 10% of the license fee; non-payment for 12 consecutive months results in registration cancellation and strike-off from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), submitted through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return, within 3 months of the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2021 and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Regulations attracts fines up to WST 100,000 (approx. USD 37,000); daily default penalties apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), International Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year; annual economic substance notification required for all international companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 500 (approx. USD 185); false or misleading information attracts penalties up to WST 10,000 (approx. USD 3,700); ongoing default may lead to information exchange and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory where the International Company is a public company, a licensed financial institution, or where annual gross revenue exceeds WST 500,000 (approx. USD 185,000) or total assets exceed WST 300,000 (approx. USD 111,000).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for larger entities; IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities (IFRS for SMEs) permitted for companies below the audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a register of significant individuals and beneficial owners at its registered office in Samoa. Any transfer of shares changing beneficial ownership must be recorded and submitted to the registered agent within 14 days; the annual beneficial ownership confirmation is filed with SIFA together with the Annual Return and must identify each member holding 25% or more of shares, direct or indirect control, and senior managing officials.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,500 per annum for licensed registered agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial services in Samoa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 - 4,000 per annum for a certified audit by a Samoan licensed auditor, applicable only if revenue/asset thresholds are exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for Samoa International Company (general Samoa corporate income tax rate: 25%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987 exempts International Companies from all Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax on profits, dividends, and distributions. The exemption requires no commercial activity in Samoa and no beneficial ownership by Samoan residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Declaration (Form IC-AD) and annual government fee via the Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFSC) electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, registration number, registered office address, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; non-resident directors may list a service address in Samoa

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, nationality, residential address of all current directors and shareholders, including nominee holders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee shareholders must identify the ultimate beneficial owner to the registered agent; the local registered agent must countersign

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of ongoing compliance with the International Companies Act, confirmation of no taxable local activities, and acknowledgement of annual fee
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be signed by a Samoan-resident director or the licensed registered agent; affix the company seal

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 100 per month or part thereof, plus an automatic late fee of WST 200. Continued failure permits strike-off and dissolution of the company; directors may be fined WST 1,000 each

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Company dividends (general Samoan statutory dividend withholding tax rate: 15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is necessary for International Companies because all dividends and profits are statutorily exempt. If a foreign investor seeks a Samoa tax residence certificate for treaty purposes, the authorised agent must submit Form T-16 (Confirmation of Residency) to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, along with the Certificate of Incorporation, a non-residence declaration, and the annual SIFSC receipt. Processing ordinarily takes 10 business days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% from an International Company. For non-exempt domestic entities, the statutory rates are 15% for royalties and 15% for interest; treaty rates may be reduced to 10% under Samoa's DTAs (e.g., with Australia and New Zealand).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory transfer-pricing documentation threshold applies to an International Company because of its zero-tax exemption. In the unlikely event an IC is found to be carrying on taxable Samoan-source activity, the Income Tax Act 2015 general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) imposes arm's length pricing on related-party transactions with a de facto materiality threshold of WST 0 for any transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not enact OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations. Nevertheless, the International Companies Act requires the maintenance of a registered agent and registered office in Samoa. To avoid reclassification by foreign tax authorities or Samoan anti-avoidance measures, the IC should demonstrate practical substance through board meeting minutes, operational decision-making, and the holding of corporate records outside the country.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company exemption while deriving income from Samoan domestic sources, or conducting prohibited local commercial activity under the International Companies Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of exempt status; immediate assessment of corporate income tax at 25% on all income, plus a 50% civil penalty and 20% per annum interest under the Tax Administration Act 2015
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; the Commissioner may issue a travel ban and asset restraint order against any director

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a registered agent address with no operational records, no board oversight, and failing to file the Annual Declaration for more than one consecutive period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative strike-off, dissolution, and a fine of up to WST 50,000 against the company; directors may be disqualified
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability to creditors for debts incurred after the shell company ceased substance; director disqualification for a minimum of 5 years and possible criminal imprisonment of up to 2 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a current beneficial ownership register or failure to perform customer due diligence (CDD) when transacting through the Samoan financial system, in breach of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and Financial Intelligence Unit directives
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to WST 1,000,000 for the entity and a further WST 500,000 for each non-compliant officer; imprisonment of up to 10 years for deliberate violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, corporate asset forfeiture, and up to 10 years imprisonment where directors knowingly participate in laundering proceeds or facilitate sanctions evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or transferring intellectual property out of the IC while the company is insolvent, or stripping assets to avoid creditor claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Voidable transaction; fine of up to WST 10,000; Court may order reinstatement of assets and immediate dissolution of the IC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to make restitution to the company, personally liable for the debts arising from the fraudulent preference, and sentenced to imprisonment of up to 5 years
